    <rect id="c-inventory" x="64" y="328" width="636" height="256" data-content="<b>1. Inventory the real delivery paths</b><br>Map repositories, CI, artifacts and deploy engines.<br>Trace dev/staging/production and manual handoffs.<br>Record desired-state ownership and target identities.<br>Prioritize gaps with application and QA teams." fill="#a0c4fb" stroke="#6a8bbf" stroke-width="2" data-text-color="#14315e" data-font-family="noto_sans" data-font-size="22" data-text-align="left" data-text-align-vertical="middle" data-miro-id="3458764690643374321" />

    <rect id="c-design" x="860" y="328" width="636" height="256" data-content="<b>2. Agree the shared release contract</b><br>Choose GitOps layout, engine and target mapping.<br>Define manifests, pinned artifacts and configuration.<br>Set PR checks, owners and promotion evidence.<br>Agree drift, migration and recovery policies." fill="#a0c4fb" stroke="#6a8bbf" stroke-width="2" data-text-color="#14315e" data-font-family="noto_sans" data-font-size="22" data-text-align="left" data-text-align-vertical="middle" data-miro-id="3458764690643374323" />

    <rect id="c-pilot" x="1656" y="328" width="636" height="256" data-content="<b>3. Prove one development release</b><br>Build a traceable immutable candidate.<br>Review desired state and reconcile a scoped target.<br>Test failures, acceptance and reported drift.<br>Exercise approved recovery and retain evidence." fill="#a0c4fb" stroke="#6a8bbf" stroke-width="2" data-text-color="#14315e" data-font-family="noto_sans" data-font-size="22" data-text-align="left" data-text-align-vertical="middle" data-miro-id="3458764690643374325" />

Extend staging and production</b><br>Promote accepted artifacts without rebuilding.<br>Validate target approvals, dependencies and checks.<br>Replace manual steps after equivalent proof.<br>Publish runbooks and assign ongoing ownership." fill="#a0c4fb" stroke="#6a8bbf" stroke-width="2" data-text-color="#14315e" data-font-family="noto_sans" data-font-size="22" data-text-align="left" data-text-align-vertical="middle" data-miro-id="3458764690643374357" />

    <rect id="c-proof" x="64" y="824" width="1432" height="224" data-content="• Trace source → immutable artifacts → GitOps revision → actual target.<br>• Deploy accepted artifacts with each target’s own configuration/checks.<br>• Failed checks, sync or acceptance stop the next promotion.<br>• Detect drift and route failed reconciliation to an owner.<br>• Prove recovery, including application/data/schema compatibility." fill="#ddddd8" stroke="#a8a8a0" stroke-width="2" data-text-color="#434339" data-font-family="noto_sans" data-font-size="22" data-text-align="left" data-text-align-vertical="middle" data-miro-id="3458764690643374364" />
    <rect id="c-dependencies" x="1656" y="824" width="1432" height="224" data-content="• Verified existing CI/deploy engines and environment/state inventory.<br>• Approved service artifacts and release manifests from 03/04.<br>• GitOps ownership/layout coordinated with 02; infrastructure controls in 01.<br>• QA/demo/pilot lifecycle in 05; runbooks and monitoring in 06/07.<br>• Repository access and execution identities coordinated with 08–10." fill="#ddddd8" stroke="#a8a8a0" stroke-width="2" data-text-color="#434339" data-font-family="noto_sans" data-font-size="22" data-text-align="left" data-text-align-vertical="middle" data-miro-id="3458764690643374365" />
    <rect id="c-controls" x="64" y="1200" width="1432" height="224" data-content="• Explicit product/target ownership and scoped reconciliation identities.<br>• Reviewed desired state, pinned artifacts and secret references.<br>• Agreed checks, acceptance evidence and promotion authority.<br>• Drift/incident handling and schema-aware fix/revert/recovery.<br>• Release records, runbook maintenance and recurring workflow review." fill="#ffe86d" stroke="#cbb333" stroke-width="2" data-text-color="#574900" data-font-family="noto_sans" data-font-size="22" data-text-align="left" data-text-align-vertical="middle" data-miro-id="3458764690643374366" />
    <rect id="c-decisions" x="1656" y="1200" width="1432" height="224" data-content="• Which GitOps area/repositories, engine and state layout are appropriate?<br>• Which branches/references map to each target, and what is automated?<br>• Which QA checks and owners authorize staging/production promotion?<br>• How do data migrations, dependencies and failure recovery work?<br>• What drift behavior, evidence retention and operational support apply?" fill="#ffe86d" stroke="#cbb333" stroke-width="2" data-text-color="#574900" data-font-family="noto_sans" data-font-size="22" data-text-align="left" data-text-align-vertical="middle" data-miro-id="3458764690643374367" />
    <rect id="c-boundaries" x="64" y="1504" width="3024" height="160" data-content="<b>Standardize the operating workflow without assuming every repository or tool changes</b><br>Apply <a href="https://opengitops.dev/">OpenGitOps principles</a> to reviewed desired state and target reconciliation. Coordinate 02–04 repository decisions while preserving source-access boundaries; consolidation is not a prerequisite.<br>Infrastructure apply, application release, target reconciliation and acceptance remain distinct. A Git revert alone does not restore database contents or prove disaster recovery." fill="#ddddd8" stroke="#a8a8a0" stroke-width="2" data-text-color="#434339" data-font-family="noto_sans" data-font-size="22" data-text-align="left" data-text-align-vertical="middle" data-miro-id="3458764690643374368" />
